issue.title: PSBT: SignPSBTInput rejects valid 65-byte taproot script signatures when PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE is absent
issue.body:
Title: PSBT: `SignPSBTInput` rejects valid 65-byte taproot script signatures when `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` is absent

## Summary

`SignPSBTInput()` (src/psbt.cpp, master 60afa0b8d71f, lines 690–712) defaults `sighash` to
`SIGHASH_DEFAULT` for taproot inputs when neither `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` nor the
`sighash_type` option is set (line 690). The "check all existing signatures" block then
requires every existing `PSBT_IN_TAP_SCRIPT_SIG` to be exactly 64 bytes:

```cpp
if (sighash == SIGHASH_DEFAULT) {
    if (!input.m_tap_key_sig.empty() && input.m_tap_key_sig.size() != 64) {
        return util::Unexpected{PSBTError::SIGHASH_MISMATCH};
    }
    for (const auto& [_, sig] : input.m_tap_script_sigs) {
        if (sig.size() != 64) return util::Unexpected{PSBTError::SIGHASH_MISMATCH};
    }
}
```

Per BIP-371, `PSBT_IN_TAP_SCRIPT_SIG` carries "the 64 or 65 byte Schnorr signature", and per
BIP-341 the signature is self-describing: a 64-byte signature implies hash_type
`SIGHASH_DEFAULT` (0x00), while a 65-byte signature carries an explicit trailing hash_type
(which must not be 0x00). A 65-byte signature with e.g. `0x01` (`SIGHASH_ALL`) is valid for
an input that carries no `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE`. BIP-174 requires finalizers to fail on
sighash mismatch only when the field is present ("The sighash type ... finalizers must fail
to finalize inputs which have signatures that do not match the specified sighash type") —
when the field is absent, no sighash has been "specified" for the input. Consensus likewise
places no per-input uniformity requirement: BIP-341 validation is per-signature, and the
valid hash_type set is {0x00, 0x01–0x03, 0x81–0x83}. Mixed sighash types within one input
are consensus-valid.

## Impact

A PSBT containing a 65-byte taproot script-path signature and no per-input sighash field can
no longer be signed further or finalized by Core:

- `FinalizePSBT` fails: it calls `SignPSBTInput` with
  `options.sighash_type = input.sighash_type` (= `std::nullopt`, psbt.cpp:811), so `sighash`
  resolves to `SIGHASH_DEFAULT` and the 65-byte signature trips `SIGHASH_MISMATCH`.
- `walletprocesspsbt` fails for any subsequent signer: adding a signature to an input that
  already holds a 65-byte script sig returns `SIGHASH_MISMATCH` before signing even starts.

So Core cannot finish a PSBT for a transaction that the network itself accepts.

## Real-world occurrence

Hit in production with a taproot-miniscript 3-of-4 (`multi_a`) wallet whose cosigners used
different default sighash types (one signer produced a 65-byte `SIGHASH_ALL` script
signature, others 64-byte `SIGHASH_DEFAULT`). The resulting transaction was broadcast and
confirmed on mainnet:

txid `4652e1c186845b2007c13bd97b85721128092cce17f376bb3dda44acf497150b` (block 970679),
input 0 witness: `[sig(65B, trailing 0x01), sig(64B), sig(64B), <empty>, script(138B),
control(65B)]` — a `multi_a(3 of 4)` script-path spend with one empty key slot.

But the PSBT could not be finalized by software linking Core's PSBT code (Nunchuk's vendored
Core, pinned at af78d36512, same check at their psbt.cpp:462-469); downstream report:
https://github.com/nunchuk-io/nunchuk-desktop/issues/137

## Origin of the check

Introduced by 15ce1bd73f in #31622 ("psbt: Enforce sighash type of signatures matches
psbt"), motivated by MuSig2 (all signers must use the same sighash) and CLI-vs-field
consistency. The PR discussion doesn't appear to consider 65-byte *script-path* signatures
in the no-sighash-field case; the application of the strict check to `m_tap_script_sigs`
under an assumed `SIGHASH_DEFAULT` looks like an unintended side effect.

## Suggested fix

In the `sighash == SIGHASH_DEFAULT` branch, treat 65-byte signatures as self-describing:
accept them when the trailing byte is a valid non-DEFAULT sighash type (`0x01–0x03`,
`0x81–0x83`), and reject only encodings that can never be valid (length not in {64, 65}, or
a 65-byte sig whose trailing byte is `0x00` or out of range). The same applies to
`m_tap_key_sig` in that branch (a key-path signature with explicit `SIGHASH_ALL` is likewise
65 bytes and currently rejected). The `else` branch (caller or field explicitly requested a
non-default sighash) should stay strict, per BIP-174.

Sketch (covers `m_tap_script_sigs`; `m_tap_key_sig` needs the analogous treatment):

```cpp
for (const auto& [_, sig] : input.m_tap_script_sigs) {
    if (sig.size() == 64) continue;
    if (sig.size() == 65 && sig.back() != SIGHASH_DEFAULT &&
        (sig.back() & ~SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY) <= SIGHASH_SINGLE) continue;
    return util::Unexpected{PSBTError::SIGHASH_MISMATCH};
}
```

Happy to turn this into a PR with a functional test (mixed-sighash taproot miniscript input)
if the approach is endorsed.

events.body:
Additional spec support for the "field absent" case, from BIP-174 itself:

- The Signer role section ("Data Signers Check For") states: *"If a sighash type is not provided, the signer should sign using SIGHASH_ALL, **but may use any sighash type they wish**."*
- The Input Finalizer role section states the must-fail rule conditionally: *"If the input has a `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` field, the Input Finalizer must fail to finalize that input if any signature does not match the specified sighash type."*

So the BIP explicitly (a) permits signatures with any sighash type when the field is absent, and (b) scopes the finalizer's must-fail obligation to inputs where the field is present. The current `SignPSBTInput` check goes beyond both when the field is absent by enforcing the locally *assumed* default (`SIGHASH_DEFAULT` for taproot) against self-describing 65-byte signatures.

(For taproot specifically, BIP-341 makes the signature itself authoritative: 64 bytes = SIGHASH_DEFAULT, 65 bytes = explicit trailing hash_type; both forms are valid in the same input, as the confirmed mainnet transaction in the OP demonstrates.)
